svg.title: Verify each step after introducing recombinant DNA
svg.desc: The recombinant-DNA workflow specifies source,insert,vector and cutting/joining predictions before introducing DNA into cells. Selection identifies a linked survival or detection feature but can retain empty-vector cells. Subsequent tests check insert presence,orientation and sequence with assay controls; then RNA,protein and biological activity are measured separately. A failed insert-specific PCR can reflect absence or assay failure. A plasmid can persist separately rather than necessarily integrate into the host chromosome. The diagram distinguishes successful uptake,selected colony,correct construct,expression and function without inventing a laboratory result.

g.text: Verify each step after introducing recombinant DNA
A successful earlier step does not establish every later claim.
Predict cuts, joining and required vector features.
Uptake can occur in only some cells.
A selectable feature can retain an empty vector too.
Check insert presence, orientation and sequence.
A failed insert assay needs positive and negative controls.
Measure RNA, protein and the intended activity.
A plasmid need not integrate into the host chromosome.
Selection ≠ correct insert ≠ expression ≠ successful biological function.
